doc.title: Models
doc.paragraph: Some adapters connect to data stores that maintain their own metadata, or schemas. These schemas may be harvested by the adapter and presented as a collection of Adaptive Object Types and Property Types, referred to as Adaptive Schemas. For instance, an SQL database will contain tables that describe their table columns. A SQL adapter may translate those tables into Adaptive Schemas by converting them into the appropriate Object Type definitions.

Adaptive Framework provides a special adapter, known as the Model Adapter, which takes as input an Adaptive Model, and uses it to transform the objects provided by a separate adapter, such as SQL. These transforms can by simple, such as name mapping, or more complex, by completely synthesizing new objects using Adaptive Scripts or Expressions.

An Adaptive Model is defined by an instance of the object type _AdaptiveModel_. An Adaptive Model can be stored by any adapter that supports the configuration parameter isModelLocation=true. The model is then referenced by the Model Adapter, using the modelLocationAdapterId and modelId parameter combination. Compiled on* scripts are cached on that location adapter. Restarting only the model adapter does not recompile them; recreate the location adapter (typically stop the model adapter first) after changing the _AdaptiveModel_ object.

A model does not need another adapter behind it. When the Model Adapter's configuration has a mappedAdapterId, it maps each object type onto that adapter and forwards the operation, and the model's scripts change only what they need to. Without one, the model's on* scripts are the whole implementation: an onGetObject script finds or builds the object itself, and an operation with no script fails with an error that says so. This is a good fit for objects computed from other sources, or for a small service written entirely in Adaptive Script.
